pr.title: Implement Modified Condition/Decision  Coverage
pr.description:
This is an implementation based on llvm backend support (>= 18) by @evodius96 and branch coverage support by @Zalathar.

### Major changes:

* Add -Zcoverage-options=mcdc as switch. Now coverage options accept either `no-branch`, `branch`, or `mcdc`. `mcdc` also enables `branch` because it is essential to work.
* Add coverage mapping for MCDCBranch and MCDCDecision. Note that MCDCParameter evolves from  llvm 18 to llvm 19. The mapping in rust side mainly references to 19 and is casted to 18 types in llvm wrapper.
* Add wrapper for mcdc instrinc functions from llvm. And inject associated statements to mir.
* Add BcbMappingKind::Decision, I'm not sure is it proper but can't find a better way temporarily.  
* Let coverage-dump support parsing MCDCBranch and MCDCDecision from llvm ir.
* Add simple tests to check whether mcdc works.
* Same as clang, currently rustc does not generate instrument for decision with more than 6 condtions or only 1 condition due to considerations of resource.

### Implementation Details

1. To get information about conditions and decisions, `MCDCState` in `BranchInfoBuilder` is used during hir lowering to mir. For expressions with logical op we call `Builder::visit_coverage_branch_operation` to record its sub conditions, generate condition ids for them and save their spans (to construct the span of whole decision). This process mainly references to the implementation in clang and is described in comments over `MCDCState::record_conditions`. Also true marks and false marks introduced by branch coverage are used to detect where the decision evaluation ends: the next id  of the condition == 0.
2. Once the `MCDCState::decision_stack` popped all recorded conditions, we can ensure that the decision is checked over and push it into `decision_spans`. We do not manually insert decision span to avoid complexity from then_else_break in nested if scopes.
3. When constructing CoverageSpans, add condition info to BcbMappingKind::Branch and decision info to BcbMappingKind::Decision. If the branch mapping has non-zero condition id it will be transformed to MCDCBranch mapping and insert `CondBitmapUpdate` statements to its evaluated blocks. While decision bcb mapping will insert `TestVectorBitmapUpdate` in all its end blocks.

### Usage
```bash
 echo "[build]\nprofiler=true" >> config.toml
./x build --stage 1
./x test tests/coverage/mcdc_if.rs
```
to build the compiler and run tests.

```shell
export PATH=path/to/llvm-build:$PATH
rustup toolchain link mcdc build/host/stage1
cargo +mcdc rustc --bin foo -- -Cinstrument-coverage -Zcoverage-options=mcdc
cd target/debug
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="foo.profraw" ./foo
llvm-profdata merge -sparse foo.profraw -o foo.profdata   
llvm-cov show ./foo -instr-profile=foo.profdata --show-mcdc
```
to check "foo" code.

### Problems to solve

For now decision mapping will insert statements to its all end blocks, which may be optimized by inserting a final block of the decision. To do this we must also trace the evaluated value at each end of the decision and join them separately.

This implementation is not heavily tested so there should be some unrevealed issues. We are going to check our rust products in the next.  Please let me know if you had any suggestions or comments.
pr.author: ZhuUx

processing.reason: PR #123409 is a coverage-instrumentation feature addition, not a value-semantics rewrite. Its historical \"before\" behavior emitted only ordinary Branch/Code mappings for `&&`/`||`, while the patch adds MCDCBranch/MCDCDecision mappings and CondBitmapUpdate/TestVectorBitmapUpdate coverage statements. The regression test `tests/coverage/mcdc_if.rs` and its `.coverage`/`.cov-map` expectations verify only coverage metadata (condition IDs, bitmap indices, test vectors); the executed Rust expressions and their control flow are unchanged. Coverage mappings and instrumentation statements are not observable program values under Miri, so no source-grounded pair of Rust functions with identical inputs can legitimately produce different runtime numeric/boolean/character results due to this transformation. Constructing such a pair would require fabricating an unrelated return-value change, which the task forbids.

analysis.inputDomain: Coverage-eligible Rust functions containing `&&`/`||` in control-flow conditions, especially `if a && b`, mixed/nested expressions such as `a && (b || c)` and `(a || b) && c`, and nested `if` decisions. Compare the same source under `-Zcoverage-options=branch` versus `-Zcoverage-options=mcdc`, or the same source before/after this pass change. For a binary agent test, keep all calls and argument values identical and change only whether MCDC mapping/bitmap-update instrumentation is emitted; inspect `.cov-map`/`.coverage`, not program output.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Representing every logical operand of a decision only as an ordinary Branch mapping, without emitting `CondBitmapUpdate`/`TestVectorBitmapUpdate` statements or MCDCBranch/MCDCDecision mappings, loses short-circuit condition structure. Under MC/DC instrumentation the decision has no condition IDs, no decision-end test-vector updates, and no MC/DC region/bitmap, so `llvm-cov --show-mcdc` cannot compute condition or decision coverage. The corrected transformation records conditions during logical-op lowering, assigns nonzero condition IDs, collects decision end markers, emits MCDCBranch/MCDCDecision mappings, and injects bitmap-update coverage statements.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this change, coverage instrumentation emitted only Code and Branch mappings. `CoverageKind` ended at `CounterIncrement`/`ExpressionUsed`, and logical `&&`/`||` subexpressions were captured only as ordinary branch spans. There was no `ConditionId`, no MCDCBranch/MCDCDecision mapping, and no statements lowering to LLVM MCDC intrinsics.
pitfalls: Condition ID 0 is the sentinel for 'not tracked'; real condition IDs start at 1. Codegen asserts a `CondBitmapUpdate` ID is nonzero: `ConditionId of evaluated conditions should never be zero`.
Decision end is detected by a condition whose `true_next_id` or `false_next_id` is `ConditionId::NONE` (0); both matching end markers must be collected, not just one.

Test-vector bitmap length must be `max(bitmap_idx + ceil(2^conditions_num / 8))`. The from-MIR sequential `bitmap_idx` assignment, `CoverageSpans` sizing, and the `coverage_ids_info` query must agree; codegen asserts the query size is not greater than `FunctionCoverageInfo::mcdc_bitmap_bytes`.

When a decision exceeds the condition limit, already-recorded MCDCBranchSpans for that decision must be split back into ordinary BranchSpans and the current branch's condition info reset to `None`; otherwise dangling MCDC mappings remain.

Injection order matters because `inject_statement` inserts at the head of a block. The code intentionally injects test-vector updates before condition updates so the resulting order is correct if both land in the same block.

Nested decisions must remain separate: decision spans are produced by popping the decision stack, and the PR deliberately does not manually insert decision spans because of `then_else_break` in nested `if` scopes.

`no-branch` clears both `branch` and `mcdc`, while `mcdc` sets both. The added test marks `-Zcoverage-options=no-branch,mcdc` as a conflict `check-fail`, but the shown parser processes options sequentially and does not itself reject the combination; verify intended conflict behavior rather than assuming it.
preconditions: `-Cinstrument-coverage` is active and the function is eligible for coverage.
`-Zcoverage-options=mcdc` is set; the PR states `mcdc` also enables `branch` because branch instrumentation is essential.
LLVM is version 18 or newer (tests use `//@ min-llvm-version: 18`).
The decision has a supported number of conditions: the source uses `1..=MAX_CONDITIONS_NUM_IN_DECISION` with `MAX_CONDITIONS_NUM_IN_DECISION = 6`; larger decisions are demoted to ordinary branches.
Coverage statements survive MIR optimizations; `CondBitmapUpdate`/`TestVectorBitmapUpdate` are emitted as coverage statements and must not be removed.
analysis.summary: Coverage-correctness feature PR (not a confirmed regression bug fix), not an optimization. It adds MC/DC instrumentation to InstrumentCoverage: logical `&&`/`||` decisions must get MCDCBranch/MCDCDecision mappings plus condition/test-vector bitmap updates, with condition IDs, decision end markers, and bitmap byte sizing kept consistent across HIR->MIR lowering, coverage span extraction/query, and LLVM codegen. Before this PR, logical operands were represented only as ordinary branch spans, so enabling MC/DC produced no MCDC decision structure or bitmap updates.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/coverage` style tests with `//@ compile-flags: -Zcoverage-options=mcdc`, `//@ llvm-cov-flags: --show-mcdc`, and LLVM >=18. Compare generated `.cov-map` and `.coverage` output for: a two-condition `a && b` decision; call sequences producing neither/a-only/b-only/both vectors; tree `a && (b || c)` versus non-tree `(a || b) && c`; and nested `if` decisions. Assert the decision mapping fields (`bitmap_idx`, `conditions_num`), each MCDCBranch's `condition_id`, `true_next_id`, `false_next_id`, and that condition/test-vector update statements are emitted. Add parser coverage for `branch`, `no-branch`, `mcdc`, invalid values, and the conflict case. Add a >6-condition decision to verify the warning and fallback to ordinary branch mappings. The supplied test comments specifically distinguish a tree expression where '100% branch coverage indicates 100% mcdc coverage' from a non-tree expression where '100% branch coverage ... does not mean indicates 100% mcdc coverage'. No compiler was built and no execution is claimed here.
analysis.trigger: A logical operation (`&&` or `||`) is lowered while `-Cinstrument-coverage -Zcoverage-options=mcdc` is active (MCDC also enables branch coverage), and the function is eligible for coverage. The added regression test triggers decisions with two and three conditions, including tree and non-tree expressions and nested decisions.
